beat: campaign structure, cups, Grand Prix, race modes, and major milestones

facts.finding: The Wii U base game (no DLC) has 8 cups of 4 tracks each = 32 tracks total. 4 'Nitro' cups of new tracks: Mushroom Cup, Flower Cup, Star Cup, Special Cup. 4 'Retro' cups of remastered classic tracks: Shell Cup, Banana Cup, Leaf Cup, Lightning Cup.
facts.source: Mario Kart Wiki/Fandom, Super Mario Wiki (mariowiki.com)
facts.notes: Shell/Banana/Leaf/Lightning Cups are NOT locked/unlockable content in MK8 (unlike some earlier titles) — they are simply the second set of Grand Prix cups you select from the same cup-select screen alongside the Nitro cups. All 8 base cups are available from the start; nothing needs to be 'unlocked' to access them.

facts.finding: At Wii U launch (May 2014), the available engine classes were 50cc, 100cc, and 150cc. Mirror Mode existed but had to be unlocked (see Mirror Mode unlock fact below). 200cc did not exist at launch.
facts.source: Wikipedia (Mario Kart 8), Perfectly Nintendo update history

facts.finding: Originally, Mirror Mode was unlocked by earning first place / a trophy in all 8 base cups at 150cc (i.e., getting gold in every 150cc cup).
facts.source: Mario Kart Racing Wiki (Fandom) 'Mirror Mode' page, cross-referenced via search summaries
facts.notes: Could not directly verify the precise wording (e.g., whether it required literal 1st place finishes in all four races of each cup, or just winning the cup trophy overall) via a fully loaded source page — the Fandom page itself returned an HTTP 402 paywall error when fetched directly, so this is based on search-result summaries only, not a directly read page. Recommend a follow-up check before finalizing wording of any related trophy.

facts.finding: 200cc was NOT in the game at launch. It was added via a free title update — Version 4.0 — released April 23, 2015 (same day as the DLC Pack 2 / Animal Crossing x Mario Kart 8 DLC). At this point, 200cc (and Mirror Mode) still had to be unlocked by the player.
facts.source: Perfectly-Nintendo.com Mario Kart 8 update history page (via search summary), Destructoid, My Nintendo News
facts.notes: This is an important version-difference: any trophy referencing 200cc or Mirror Mode should note it requires the game to be patched (title updates are built into all physical/digital copies sold after mid-2015, but a fresh unpatched cart from launch stock or an offline console would not have it).

facts.finding: Version 4.1 update, released May 1, 2015, made both 200cc and Mirror Mode available by default in Grand Prix mode without needing to unlock them (removed the unlock requirement entirely going forward).
facts.source: My Nintendo News 'Mario Kart 8 Update Version 4.1', Perfectly Nintendo, Destructoid
facts.notes: So there are actually two distinct patch milestones: v4.0 (added 200cc, still locked) and v4.1 one week later (unlocked by default for everyone). A game on the latest patch (which virtually all played copies will be, since Wii U eShop and disc-based patching requires internet at some point) will have 200cc and Mirror Mode available from a fresh save with no unlock condition at all. This affects whether 'unlock Mirror Mode' or 'unlock 200cc' can even be framed as a trophy milestone — on a fully updated game there is nothing to unlock.

facts.finding: Each Grand Prix cup, at each engine class, is awarded a star rank of 0-3 stars based on total points across its 4 races (out of a max 60 points = 15/race for 1st place). 60 points = 3 stars, 57-59 = 2 stars, 54-56 = 1 star, below 54 = 0 stars (no star awarded, cup still 'cleared'/trophy still won if you place high enough for a podium finish overall).
facts.source: GameFAQs Mario Kart 8 Q&A, Zero1Magazine, Mario Kart Racing Wiki 'Star Rank' page

facts.finding: Star ranks earned are displayed as star icons directly on the cup-selection screen for Grand Prix mode, per cup. This is a persistent, visible in-game tracker of per-cup performance history.
facts.source: GameFAQs Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Q&A thread describing the analogous MK8 mechanic; cross-referenced against MK8 (Wii U) Q&A on star meaning
facts.notes: Direct confirmation is strongest for Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's version of this screen (which is known to carry over from the Wii U original), but I could not find a screenshot-verified source specific to the original Wii U UI. High confidence the underlying star-rank display mechanic exists in Wii U MK8 (it's the same base game), medium confidence on exact UI presentation details.

facts.finding: With 8 base cups and (post-update) 5 engine classes (50cc, 100cc, 150cc, Mirror, 200cc), fully completing every cup at every class = 40 individual Grand Prix clears (8 cups x 5 classes) on Wii U base game, pre-DLC.
facts.source: Derived arithmetic from confirmed cup count (8) and confirmed engine class count (5, post-v4.1 update)
facts.notes: This is my own calculation, not a direct source statement — flagging as medium/derived. If DLC cups are included this number rises (another scout's beat).

facts.finding: Earning gold (1st place trophy) in every Grand Prix cup at 150cc and at Mirror Mode unlocks a different/extended ending credits sequence and song, plus different single-player and multiplayer title screen presentations.
facts.source: Search-result summary only (ChapterCheats/Cheats.co aggregation); could not verify against a primary or wiki source directly
facts.notes: This claim needs verification before being used as the basis for a trophy. It's a commonly repeated community claim but I was not able to confirm it against a reliable wiki page directly (e.g., mariowiki.com credits page). Treat as unconfirmed.

facts.topic: Battle Mode in original Wii U MK8 (launch)
facts.finding: At launch, Battle Mode had only ONE mode: Balloon Battle (Coin Runners and other historical battle modes were removed/absent). Crucially, Battle Mode did NOT use dedicated battle arenas — it reused 8 existing Grand Prix race tracks as battle 'courses': Mario Circuit, Toad Harbor, Moo Moo Meadows (Wii), Toad's Turnpike (N64), Sherbet Land (GCN), Donut Plains 3 (SNES), Dry Dry Desert (GCN), and Yoshi Valley (N64).
facts.source: Kotaku 'A Defense Of Mario Kart 8's Unpopular Battle Mode', Nintendo Life forum thread 'No Battle Arenas for Mario Kart DLC?', general search summaries
facts.notes: This was a well-documented, widely-reported launch criticism at the time (confirmed by multiple outlets). The exact list of the 8 specific race tracks used for battle is medium confidence — pulled from a single aggregated search summary, not cross-verified against a dedicated wiki table. Recommend a direct wiki check before finalizing which 8 tracks are used for Battle in a trophy description.

facts.finding: Could not confirm whether any Wii U update ever added new/dedicated battle arenas to the original MK8. The consensus across sources is that the original Wii U version NEVER received dedicated battle arenas — that fix only arrived with the ground-up Battle Mode redesign in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (Switch, 2017), which is a different game/product from vanilla Wii U MK8.
facts.source: Wikipedia (Mario Kart 8), Kotaku, Nintendo Life
facts.notes: Important version-difference: do NOT confuse vanilla Wii U MK8 Battle Mode with MK8 Deluxe's 5-ruleset (Balloon Battle, Bob-omb Blast, Shine Thief, Coin Runners, Renegade Roundup) dedicated-arena Battle Mode — those Deluxe features are NOT present in the Wii U original at any patch level, as far as I could confirm.

facts.finding: Mario Kart 8 (Wii U) includes one Staff Ghost per track (developer-recorded target time) for Time Trial mode. Unlike some earlier MK titles, MK8 (Wii U) does NOT have a separate tier of 'Expert'/'Fast' Staff Ghosts — just the single standard staff ghost per course.
facts.source: Mario Kart Racing Wiki 'Staff Ghosts' page (via search summary)
facts.notes: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe later added separate 150cc and 200cc staff ghosts, but that's Deluxe-specific and not part of the Wii U original per this source.

facts.finding: Could not confirm any in-game UI element that shows the player, at a glance, which tracks' staff ghosts have been beaten across all 32 base tracks (e.g., no confirmed 'completion percentage' or checklist screen for Time Trial staff-ghost beats).
facts.source: GameFAQs Q&A thread titled 'Is there an easy way to see on which Time Trials you've beaten the staff ghost?' (implies the answer is 'not easily' / no dedicated tracker)
facts.notes: This is a load-bearing gap: if there is no in-game way to see aggregate staff-ghost-beaten progress, a trophy for 'beat all staff ghosts' is still trackable per-track (each track's Time Trial leaderboard would show your ghost beat the staff ghost time), but there's no single global counter/summary screen confirmed. Flagging as a gap for the downstream design step.

facts.finding: Mario Kart 8 (Wii U) supported online races, online leaderboards, and online ghost data exchange via Nintendo Network. All of this went offline permanently on April 8, 2024 (4pm PT / 7pm ET / 12am April 9 GMT), when Nintendo shut down all Wii U and 3DS online services network-wide.
facts.source: TheSixthAxis, Neoseeker, GamesRadar+, Engadget, My Nintendo News
facts.notes: CRITICAL for trophy design: any trophy tied to online races, online leaderboard rank, downloading/uploading ghost data via Nintendo Network, or Mario Kart TV online sharing is now permanently unachievable on original hardware without unofficial server workarounds. Local wireless/LAN play and offline Time Trial/Grand Prix are unaffected. Flag any such trophy candidate for removal or reframing as local-only.

facts.topic: DLC packs (existence only, not deep content — per instructions)
facts.finding: Two paid DLC packs existed for Wii U MK8: Pack 1 'The Legend of Zelda x Mario Kart 8' (released Nov 13, 2014) adding Egg Cup and Triforce Cup (8 tracks); Pack 2 'Animal Crossing x Mario Kart 8' (released April 23, 2015, same day as the 200cc update) adding Crossing Cup and Bell Cup (8 tracks). Total with both DLC packs: 12 cups / 48 tracks.
facts.source: Forbes, Mario Kart Wiki/Fandom, RPGGeek, IBTimes
facts.notes: Per task instructions, not deep-diving DLC content — another scout covers that beat. Noting only cup names/existence/dates for structural completeness.

facts.finding: Grand Prix races in Mario Kart 8 (Wii U) feature 12 racers (up from 8 in some earlier MK titles), consistent across all engine classes.
facts.source: General series knowledge cross-referenced in search summaries (not independently re-verified with a dedicated search this session)
facts.notes: This is a widely known fact about MK8 but I did not run a dedicated confirming search this session — flagging as medium/low-effort verification. Should be easy to confirm with a single follow-up search if load-bearing for a trophy.

versionNotes.note: 200cc engine class was NOT present at Wii U launch (May 2014). Added via free Version 4.0 update on April 23, 2015 (still had to be unlocked at that point).
Version 4.1 update (May 1, 2015) made both 200cc and Mirror Mode available by default from a fresh save, removing the prior unlock requirement entirely.

Battle Mode in the original Wii U MK8 is a stripped-down, single-ruleset (Balloon Battle only) mode that reuses ordinary race tracks instead of dedicated arenas — this was a major, widely-reported launch criticism. This is fundamentally different from Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's Battle Mode (5 rulesets, dedicated arenas), which is a different product/platform (Switch) and should not be conflated when building a Wii U-specific trophy list.

All Nintendo Network online features (online races, online leaderboards, Mario Kart TV online ghost sharing) were permanently shut down April 8, 2024. Any trophy referencing online play/ranks on original Wii U hardware is now unachievable through official means.
